dimensions.title: Visualization correctness & data-viz integrity
dimensions.summary: Palimpsest's visualizations are, for the most part, faithful renderers of real backend data with strong coordinate discipline: canvas heatmaps read little-endian Float32 buffers in documented C order, char/paragraph/chunk axes are consciously distinguished, min-width rect guards prevent sub-pixel bands from vanishing, and the PCA/k-means backend is explicitly deterministic with sign-canonicalization and no-silent-cap sampling. The most material integrity gap is color-scale honesty for cosine: the two primary heatmaps (DotplotView TextHiC, ComparativeDotplot) feed raw cosine [-1,1] into a [0,1]-clamping color ramp and label the legend "0...1 similarity," while the very same repo maps cosine correctly as (x+1)/2 in LayerStatsPanel — an internal inconsistency, not ignorance. A second real defect: the phyletic-tree layout collapses to a single overlapping row for the standing 2-member validation collection because it assumes internal nodes are never leaves. Everything else audited (BlockMap, OverviewBar barcode, conservation/repeat lanes, alignment overlays, distance histograms) renders real data honestly.
strengths: Backend viz compute is genuinely deterministic and honest about degradation: analytics.py canonicalizes PCA component signs (_canonicalize_signs, analytics.py:52-60) so scatter plots are reproducible across BLAS/platforms; k-means is seeded with tie-breaking to lowest index; and sampling/block-reduction report the realized count via X-Matrix-Reduced / sampled_pairs headers rather than silently truncating (analytics.py:14-15, server.py:1686-1691).

Index-alignment contract is explicit and preserved end-to-end: analytics.py's module docstring (lines 6-9) documents that row i == chunk i and only order=cluster permutes (returning the permutation via X-Matrix-Order so cells map back to chunks), preventing silent document mislabeling.

Coordinate axes are consciously distinguished, not conflated: DotplotView labels axes as chunk indices with an explicit comment 'Axis labels — chunk indices, not paragraph indices' (DotplotView.tsx:401) and aria-label states '{n}x{n} chunks ({chunkSize} words each)'; ComparativeDotplot correctly labels paragraph axes '¶N' matching the backend's paragraph-embedding matrix (cross_similarity.py:21-24).

The correct cosine [-1,1]->[0,1] transform DOES exist in the codebase (LayerStatsPanel.tsx:174 'row.push((flat[i*dim+j] + 1) / 2)'), proving the team knows the honest mapping — the primary heatmaps simply don't reuse it.

SVG rect math consistently guards against invisible bands via Math.max(1, ...) width floors (OverviewBar.tsx:37,58; CorpusView.tsx:81,225,256; LayerLane.tsx:73), and distance histograms clip float-error excursions back into [0,2] with an explicit comment that np.histogram would otherwise silently undercount (analytics.py:212-216).

findings.title: TextHiC heatmap legend claims '0...1 similarity' but renders raw cosine [-1,1] through a [0,1]-clamping ramp
findings.evidence: DotplotView.tsx:26 interpolateColor clamps `Math.max(0, Math.min(1, value))`; legend at DotplotView.tsx:796-806 hardcodes labels '0' ... '1' ... 'similarity'. Backend _cosine_matrix returns values clipped to [-1,1] (self_similarity.py:119 `np.clip(matrix, -1.0, 1.0)`). Empirically the live Matthew/Mark embedding heatmap (GET /api/projects/.../embedding/871a3ae739394b3b/heatmap) has min offdiag=0.529, max=1.0 — so the entire lower ~53% of the color ramp is dead and every cell reads as 'high similarity', a compressed/misleading dynamic range. For other embedding models negative cosines would be silently floored to white (indistinguishable from 'similarity 0').
findings.recommendation: Map cosine metrics honestly before coloring, reusing the existing LayerStatsPanel.tsx:174 transform `(v+1)/2`, and either relabel the legend '-1 ... 1 (cosine)' or auto-fit the ramp to the observed [min,max] with the range printed in the legend. Word-overlap/jaccard are genuinely [0,1] and can keep the current mapping; gate the transform on metric family.
findings.verify_reasoning:
Core mechanism CONFIRMED at the code level. DotplotView.tsx:26 interpolateColor clamps `Math.max(0, Math.min(1, value))`; the legend (DotplotView.tsx:798/805/806) hardcodes '0' … '1' … 'similarity'. The data path (DotplotView.tsx:314) sets signal.data directly from the raw self_similarity `.bin` buffer, and DotplotView.tsx:377/393 pass those raw values straight into interpolateColor with NO cosine transform. Backend _cosine_matrix (self_similarity.py:114-120) stores cosine RAW in [-1,1] (`np.clip(matrix, -1.0, 1.0)`), whereas jaccard/word_overlap/edit_distance builders genuinely produce [0,1] (lines 128, 153, 208). So for the cosine metric specifically, DotplotView's [0,1] clamp is applied to a [-1,1] signal: the [0, observed-min] portion of the ramp is dead and any negative cosine would floor to white — the finding's mechanism is accurate. The recommended fix is also sound: LayerStatsPanel.tsx:174 already does `(flat[...]+1)/2 // cosine [-1,1] → [0,1]` for the sibling embedding-heatmap render path, so a gated `(v+1)/2` for the cosine family plus an honest legend is a minimal, existing-pattern change.

Empirical range CONFIRMED but the cited endpoint MISATTRIBUTED (why this is 'partial', not 'confirmed'): I hit GET /api/projects/{geneva-mm}/embedding/871a3ae739394b3b/heatmap on the live :8092 server (X-Matrix-N 391, 611524 bytes) and computed min offdiag=0.5293, max=1.0, mean=0.843, 99% of offdiag in [0.67,0.92] — reproducing the '0.529…1.0' figure almost exactly and showing the lower ~53% of a [0,1] ramp is unused. BUT that endpoint feeds LayerStatsPanel, which ALREADY applies the (v+1)/2 transform correctly (LayerStatsPanel.tsx:174) — it is NOT the DotplotView render path and is NOT buggy. The finding uses a non-buggy sibling path as proof of the buggy path. DotplotView's actual data source is /api/projects/{id}/self_similarity/cs/{cs}/cosine, which is NOT materialized in the validation workspace (chunk_sizes:[] for both MM projects, embeddings/status available:false on the standalone project), so I could not directly render DotplotView showing the compressed ramp — the code path is unambiguous but the live proof is by analogy. Two further overstatements: (a) 'negative cosines silently floored to white' is LATENT not observed — the real MLX data has zero negative offdiag values (min 0.529), so the practical harm here is compressed dynamic range, not sign-flip-to-white; (b) mitigating factors the finding omits: the hover tooltip shows the raw value to 3 decimals (DotplotView.tsx:763, aria-label 973) and the active metric name is displayed (line 791), so exact values remain inspectable. Note the threshold slider (default 0, DotplotView.tsx:219/817) also filters on raw cosine (line 376/390), so its 0-100% semantics are likewise skewed for cosine — a related, unmentioned symptom that mildly reinforces the finding.

Severity: this is a genuine data-viz-integrity defect (misleading legend + compressed/potentially-sign-losing ramp on the cosine metric), but it is a display-layer cosmetic issue confined to one metric family, raw values are recoverable via tooltip, no negative-flooring is actually occurring on real data, and the fix is a known one-liner. High overstates it; I adjust to medium. Grounding: read DotplotView.tsx:1-60/210-328/760-812, self_similarity.py:114-212, LayerStatsPanel.tsx:160-186, server.py:1474-1481/1663-1694; hit live :8092 heatmap and computed the matrix stats with numpy.

findings.title: Phyletic tree collapses to a single overlapping row for the standing 2-member collection (root-leaf treated as non-leaf)
findings.evidence: layoutTree (corpusOverview.ts:143-159) increments leafCounter only for nodes with `children.length===0`. Live GET /api/collections/matthew-mark-validation/phyletic-tree returns a degenerate NJ tree where leaf A has parent=null (is the root) and leaf B has parent=A. Simulating layoutTree on this exact topology yields leafCount=1, so both members get y=0.5 (corpusOverview.ts:164 `leafCount>1 ? ... : 0.5`) — they render on the same horizontal line. PhyleticTreeView (CorpusView.tsx:182-194) draws both member labels, which overlap.
findings.recommendation: Count leaves by `is_leaf` (which the backend supplies) rather than `children.length===0`, or insert a synthetic root above two-taxon trees. Add a viz test for the 2-member NJ case; it's the exact shape of the standing validation collection.
findings.verify_reasoning: Verified end-to-end against live API and source. (1) GET :8092/api/collections/matthew-mark-validation/phyletic-tree returns exactly the described topology: node A parent=null, children=[B], is_leaf=true; node B parent=A, children=[], is_leaf=true — both leaves carry member ids. (2) layoutTree at browser/src/components/CorpusView/corpusOverview.ts:143-159 increments leafCounter only when node.children.length===0 (line 148); on this topology only B qualifies, so leafCount=1. Line 164 `y: leafCount > 1 ? (yPos.get(n.id) ?? 0)/(leafCount-1) : 0.5` therefore assigns y=0.5 to BOTH nodes. (3) Render side confirmed: CorpusView.tsx:156 py(y)=14+y*(H-28) puts both at the same vertical center, and lines 182-194 draw a label for every node with a member, so both labels overlap. All cited file:line references are exact. (4) This is not a data fluke: phylo.py:64-65 shows NJ returns a single edge with NO internal node for n==2, and root_tree (phylo.py:107-136) then makes one leaf the root — so the degenerate root-leaf-with-one-leaf-child shape is structurally guaranteed for EVERY 2-member collection, which is precisely the shape of the standing matthew-mark-validation collection. (5) Test-gap claim verified: the sole layoutTree test (corpusOverview.test.ts:71-90) uses a 3-taxon tree yielding leafCount=2, never exercising the `: 0.5` degenerate branch; the 2-member case is untested. Baseline vitest for this file is green (9/9). Adjusting severity high->medium: the defect is real, deterministic, and hits the flagship validation collection, but it is a bounded visualization-legibility collapse (overlapping labels) with no data-integrity, crash, or security impact — the underlying distances/tree JSON are correct and labels remain individually clickable via SVG order. The recommended fix (count leaves by is_leaf, which TreeNode already carries at corpusOverview.ts:40, or insert a synthetic root above two-taxon trees) is directly implementable; note a pure is_leaf count still needs the y-assignment to separate a root-leaf from its child-leaf, so the synthetic-root option is the more complete remedy.

findings.title: ComparativeDotplot applies a hidden `value < 0.1` similarity floor with no legend or disclosure
findings.evidence: ComparativeDotplot.tsx:123 `if (value < 0.1) continue;` silently drops all cross-similarity cells below 0.1, and interpolateColor (ComparativeDotplot.tsx:16-27) clamps [0,1] while the backend cross-matrix is cosine clipped to [-1,1] (cross_similarity.py:104). There is no legend at all on this chart and no on-screen note that a floor is applied, so negative and low-positive paragraph pairs render identically to 'no data' background (#f8f8f8). The score-threshold slider only affects the orange alignment overlays, not the underlying heatmap floor.
findings.recommendation: Add a color legend to ComparativeDotplot, expose or remove the 0.1 floor, and apply the (x+1)/2 cosine mapping so the heatmap distinguishes 'dissimilar' from 'unrendered'.

findings.title: EmbeddingLane min-max normalizes an unbounded, right-skewed nn-density scalar, skewing the color ramp toward light
findings.evidence: EmbeddingLane (LayerLane.tsx:112-121) min-max normalizes then ramps via rampBlue. The default encoding is nn-density = inverse NN cosine distance `1/(dist+eps)` (analytics.py:256), which is unbounded above. Empirically on the live layer (GET .../lane?encoding=nn-density, n=391): min=5.53, max=33.44, median=13.74 — the median chunk lands at only 0.29 on the [min,max] ramp, so a majority of chunks read as pale. A single very-dense chunk (dist→0) would blow up max and wash out the whole lane.
findings.recommendation: Normalize nn-density on a robust scale (e.g. percentile clip at p95, or log/rank transform) and note the transform in the aria-label, so one dense outlier can't dominate the ramp.

findings.title: EmbeddingLane 'cluster' encoding renders categorical cluster IDs through a sequential blue ramp, implying false ordinal magnitude
findings.evidence: lane_encoding returns k-means cluster ids as float32 for encoding='cluster' (analytics.py:250-251), and EmbeddingLane feeds any scalar through the sequential rampBlue after min-max (LayerLane.tsx:118-121). A categorical id (cluster 3 vs cluster 1) thus gets a darker-vs-lighter blue, falsely encoding order/distance between nominal clusters. Reachable via /lane?encoding=cluster; the default UI path uses nn-density (embedding_track.py:209), so this is latent rather than always-on.
findings.recommendation: Detect categorical encodings (cluster) in EmbeddingLane and use a qualitative palette (distinct hues per id) rather than a sequential ramp; keep sequential only for pc1/nn-density.

findings.title: charts.tsx generic Heatmap hardcodes a [0,1] assumption in its own comment and clamp
findings.evidence: charts.tsx:191 comment 'Values assumed in [0,1]; deeper = higher' and charts.tsx:205 `Math.max(0, Math.min(1, v))`. This component is fed by LayerStatsPanel which DOES pre-map cosine via (x+1)/2 (LayerStatsPanel.tsx:174), so it's currently correct there — but the component silently trusts its caller with no range assertion, so any future caller passing raw cosine would be silently distorted (the same class of bug already live in DotplotView).
findings.recommendation: Either accept an explicit [min,max] domain prop on Heatmap or document the contract as load-bearing; consider a dev assertion when values fall outside [0,1].

findings.title: EmbeddingScatter auto-scales X and Y axes independently, distorting PCA variance aspect ratio
findings.evidence: EmbeddingScatter.tsx:46-51 computes separate sx=(maxX-minX) and sy=(maxY-minY) and stretches each axis to fill the square canvas. PC1 carries more variance than PC2 by construction, but independent per-axis scaling makes PC2 spread visually equal to PC1, so semantically round clusters appear stretched and inter-cluster distances are anisotropically distorted. No axis ticks or scale are shown, so a viewer cannot recover true proportions.
findings.recommendation: Use a single shared scale (equal units on both axes, letterboxing the shorter axis) so PCA geometry is preserved, and/or annotate the explained-variance ratio per axis.

dimensions.title: UX & end-to-end workflow completeness
dimensions.summary: Palimpsest's single-text journey (import → sections → tracks → reading/browser/analysis/dotplot) and the collections workbench (Compare, Corpus with Overview/Members/Corpus/Masking/Analyses/Sweep/Probe) are genuinely mature and mostly complete, with strong empty/loading/error states and an unusually disciplined cost-confirmation culture in the collections tier (Probe, Sweep, Reconcile all gate expensive work behind a CostDialog and never auto-run). The main friction is at the seams: the cross-text mental model (Project vs Collection) is under-signposted — the Corpus tab is absent from the Home launchpad and can only be reached after opening a single text, and the corpus-graph auto-builds without the cost discipline applied elsewhere. A few analysis dead-ends tell the scholar to "run analysis first" with no in-place CTA, and the embedding cost estimate the backend already computes is never surfaced in the UI. These are polish gaps on top of a real, working product, not structural holes.
strengths: Cost/confirm discipline in the collections tier is exemplary and consistent: ProbePanel runs a free ref-lookup directly but gates the expensive text-embedding probe behind CostDialog with explicit 'runs only when you confirm' copy (ProbePanel.tsx:71-76, 201-212); SweepPanel shows the exact pre-run member-pair count and states 'Nothing runs until you click Run' (SweepPanel.tsx:209-219); CorpusView's reconcile flow explains the per-member re-embed cost before acting (CorpusView.tsx:480-506).

Honesty about analytical limits is surfaced in the UI rather than hidden: AnalysesPanel renders the diffusion metric's non_directional_note verbatim so the tool never implies an 'A influenced B' causal claim (AnalysesPanel.tsx:141-143); SweepPanel/ProbePanel show empirical recall as 'n/a' when the oracle was unsampled instead of a fake number (sweep.ts:5-7); AnalysisPanel exposes clamped/effective/requested params and silent HMM->KMeans fallbacks (AnalysisPanel.tsx:59-68).

Empty, loading, and error states are handled across nearly every view: CompareView distinguishes no-project / no-secondary / ready-to-align / computing states with tailored copy and a shimmer bar (CompareView.tsx:220-257); Synteny/Circos/Diff each have their own empty state; CorpusView shows a graph gate only for graph-dependent sub-tabs (CorpusView.tsx:47-48, 438-440).

The metric-congruence contract has a first-class UI affordance: CongruenceBadge asks the backend whether members are comparable on the chosen metric and offers a reconcile action rather than silently comparing across incompatible embedding spaces (CongruenceBadge.tsx:1-47; live /congruence returns needs_embedding:true for the validation collection).

The subtext-derivation journey is a complete 3-step wizard (pick layers -> refine elements -> generate) with live SSE progress and optional routing into a chosen or auto-created collection (SubtextWizard.tsx:2-6, 104-117, 386-388), tying the single-text and collection tiers together coherently.

findings.title: DotplotView dead-ends on 'Run analysis first' with no way to run it
findings.evidence: browser/src/components/DotplotView/DotplotView.tsx:325 sets error 'Self-similarity matrix not available. Run analysis first.'; rendered as a terminal centered message at line 945 with no button/link. The self_similarity track producer lives on a different tab (Analysis > Tracks).
findings.recommendation: Turn the dead-end into an actionable CTA: render a 'Compute self-similarity' button that either POSTs /analyze/self_similarity for this project or switches to the Analysis tab with that track pre-focused. Otherwise a scholar who launches TextHiC on an un-analyzed text is stranded with instructions but no controls.
findings.verify_reasoning:
Core claim confirmed by code + live server. DotplotView.tsx:325 sets 'Self-similarity matrix not available. Run analysis first.' and line 945 renders it as a terminal centered message (text-[#b91c1c]) with no button or link; the toolbar (lines 759-789) and error branch contain no CTA. I reproduced the trigger on live server :8092: GET /data/{douay-rheims...}/signals/self_similarity.json returns 404 ({"detail":"File not found"}), which flows line 258 (throw 'not found') -> line 324 catch -> line 325 setError. The texthic/TextHiC tab is ungated (TabBar.tsx:7 'Alt+3'; ProjectPicker.tsx:298), so a scholar can genuinely land here on an un-analyzed text and be stranded. The producer really is on another surface: AnalysisPanel's SelfSimilarityParamDialog (AnalysisPanel.tsx:955-960), on the Analysis tab.

However, the auditor's primary recommendation ('render a Compute self-similarity button that POSTs /analyze/self_similarity for this project') is technically unsound: per AnalysisPanel.tsx:189-191 and 879-883, self_similarity 'has no runnable defaults -- it requires an explicit input bundle, so [a bare run] is guaranteed-400'. The real producer endpoint is POST /api/projects/{id}/analyze/{track} but it needs an explicit layer bundle chosen in the dialog. Only the auditor's ALTERNATIVE (switch to Analysis tab with the track pre-focused / open the config dialog) is implementable. Feasibility of that fix is high: useViewStore with setActiveTab('analysis') is already imported at DotplotView.tsx:2, and /self_similarity/inputs returns 200 for discovery.

Severity: real UX friction, not a correctness/data/security defect. Nothing breaks or is lost, and the message ('Run analysis first') does instruct the user, just without a control; a knowledgeable user reaches the Analysis tab. High overstates it. Adjusting to medium.

findings.title: Corpus tab is unreachable from the landing page and requires opening a single text first
findings.evidence: ProjectPicker TOOLS launchpad lists only 6 tools and omits 'corpus' (ProjectPicker.tsx:295-302), while TabBar exposes all 7 including Corpus (TabBar.tsx:11). AppLayout gates the entire tabbed shell — including the cross-text corpus/compare views — on a single active project's metadata (AppLayout.tsx:60-62), and the default tab is 'reading' (viewStore.ts:49).
findings.recommendation: Add a Corpus/Collections entry to the Home launchpad that opens a collection workbench directly, and let the Corpus tab load with no active single project (it already fetches its own collections list). As-is, the cross-text (Collection) mental model is a hidden second-class citizen behind the single-text (Project) model — a scholar must open some arbitrary text just to reach corpus-wide analysis.
findings.verify_reasoning:
Every cited fact checks out against the code I read:

1. ProjectPicker TOOLS launchpad (browser/src/components/common/ProjectPicker.tsx:295-302) lists exactly 6 tools — reading, browser, texthic, characters, analysis, compare — and omits 'corpus'. CONFIRMED verbatim.
2. TabBar (browser/src/components/Layout/TabBar.tsx:4-12) exposes all 7 tabs including {id:'corpus', shortcut:'Alt+7'}. CONFIRMED.
3. AppLayout gates the ENTIRE tabbed shell on a single active project: line 30 derives metadata = projects[activeProjectId]?.metadata; lines 60-62 return <ProjectPicker/> whenever !metadata. So TabBar (line 96) and CorpusView (line 127) never mount without an active single project. CONFIRMED.
4. Default tab is 'reading' (viewStore.ts:49). CONFIRMED.
5. The recommendation's premise — CorpusView 'already fetches its own collections list' and could load standalone — is accurate. CorpusView.tsx:292-305 runs reloadCollections() on mount, fetching /api/collections and auto-selecting the first usable collection (line 297); it reads from useCollectionStore/collectionStore (line 15, 269-273), NOT from the active project. Its only activeProjectId use (line 354) is an on-demand cell-click jump to the Compare dotplot, not a render prerequisite.

I confirmed there is genuinely no alternate path to the corpus tab: AppLayout honors only a ?project= URL param (line 49-53), no ?tab= deep-link; the Alt+7 keyboard shortcut (keyboard.ts:120-122) only works after the shell mounts, which requires metadata; launchTool()/TOOLS never passes 'corpus'; and openCollection() (ProjectPicker.tsx:595-599) merely filters BookCovers to a library page, where clicking a cover calls handleSelect → loadProject (single text). So reaching corpus requires: open some arbitrary single text, then click Corpus/Alt+7.

Live API grounds the standalone claim: GET http://localhost:8092/api/collections returns the standing 'matthew-mark-validation' collection (2 projects) with no project context; /api/projects returns 3. The corpus data source is reachable independently of any active project.

Adversarial cross-check that strengthens rather than refutes: Compare (CompareView.tsx) is the sibling cross-text/N-text view and it IS in the launchpad AND ships its own in-view project/collection picker (CompareProjectPicker, lines 35-40, fetches projects+collections, scope by collection). Corpus is architecturally the same class of cross-text tool with its own reloadCollections but is the single tab excluded from the launchpad — evidence the omission is an inconsistency, not a deliberate design.

Severity adjusted high->medium. It is a real, grounded second-class-citizen problem for the entire collections/corpus tier (a headline C1-C7 / FR-33/FR-38 capability), but it is navigation friction, not broken functionality or data loss: the corpus tab is reachable in ~2 clicks, and collections ARE surfaced elsewhere on the landing page (sidebar 'My Collections' NavRows at ProjectPicker.tsx:720-730, plus BookCover add-to-collection). The finding's 'hidden second-class citizen' framing is mildly overstated — collections appear prominently in the sidebar; what is actually gated behind opening an arbitrary text is specifically the corpus-analysis workbench entry point.

findings.title: corpus-graph auto-builds on every collection selection with no cost confirmation, breaking the tier's own discipline
findings.evidence: CorpusView.loadOverview POSTs /collections/{id}/corpus-graph unconditionally (CorpusView.tsx:311) fired by a useEffect on collectionId change (CorpusView.tsx:340-342). This is the all-pairs homology assembly (union-find over candidate generation) yet shows only 'Assembling graph…' (line 382) — no CostDialog, unlike Probe/Sweep/Reconcile which all gate on cost.
findings.recommendation: For collections beyond a small member/pair threshold, gate the initial corpus-graph build behind the same CostDialog used elsewhere (show member and pair counts), or make the first build an explicit 'Build corpus graph' button. Silently launching potentially O(N^2) work on tab entry is inconsistent with the surrounding honesty guarantees.

findings.title: Backend embedding cost estimate exists but is never shown; EmbeddingDialog hard-codes a guess
findings.evidence: GET /api/projects/{id}/embedding/estimate?chunk_label=... returns {chunk_count:391, total_chars:204936, estimated_seconds:9.8} (live probe). No frontend code calls it (grep of browser/src finds zero uses). EmbeddingDialog instead prints a static 'This typically takes 10-30 seconds' (AnalysisPanel.tsx:486-489), and handleRunAll fires /embeddings/compute with no cost surface at all (AnalysisPanel.tsx:634).
findings.recommendation: Fetch /embedding/estimate for the active chunk label and render the real chunk_count / estimated_seconds inside EmbeddingDialog, and show the same estimate before 'Compute All' triggers embeddings. The data is already computed server-side; wiring it in closes the single-text pre-run cost gap that the collections tier already solved.

findings.title: No way to add or remove collection members from inside the Corpus workbench
findings.evidence: MembersPanel offers only role toggle and open-member (MembersPanel.tsx:104-146); it has no add/remove affordance. Add-to-collection lives only in ProjectPicker's per-book overflow menu (ProjectPicker.tsx:205, 581-593), and there is no remove-from-collection UI anywhere despite DELETE /api/collections/{id}/projects/{project_id} existing (server endpoint list).
findings.recommendation: Add 'Add member' (project picker) and 'Remove' controls to MembersPanel so a scholar can curate a collection while analyzing it, instead of context-switching back to the library landing page. The remove endpoint already exists but is UI-orphaned.

findings.title: Corpus 'Masking' sub-tab shows only a read-only conservation lane, not a cross-text masking editor
findings.evidence: CorpusView 'masking' sub-tab renders solely a ConservationLane from root-track when graph && rootTrack (CorpusView.tsx:470-477). The backend exposes cross-text-mask/{member}, liftover, and mask-effect endpoints (server endpoint list) that have no UI here. A scholar reading the tab label 'Masking' expects controls to mask/liftover across texts.
findings.recommendation: Either surface the cross-text mask + liftover + mask-effect capabilities in this sub-tab (with the same overlay-editor pattern the single-text MaskingPanel uses), or rename the sub-tab to 'Conservation' so its label matches the read-only content and doesn't imply missing editing affordances.

findings.title: Probe 'existing passage' mode requires typing a raw chunk index with no passage preview
findings.evidence: ProbePanel ref mode exposes a bare numeric 'Chunk index' input (ProbePanel.tsx:116-125) with no way to see which passage a given index maps to; the scholar must guess or already know the integer offset.
findings.recommendation: Replace/augment the raw index input with a passage picker or a preview of the chunk text at the selected index (the chunk store is already server-side accessible), so the ref-probe query is chosen by content rather than by memorized offset.

findings.title: Sweep-run delete fires immediately with no confirmation
findings.evidence: SweepPanel deleteRun DELETEs /collections/{id}/sweep/{run_id} on click with no confirm step (SweepPanel.tsx:139-149, button at 282-288), unlike ProjectPicker's delete which requires an in-menu confirm (ProjectPicker.tsx:231-239).
findings.recommendation: Add a lightweight confirm (inline 'Delete?' toggle) for consistency. Low severity because the panel documents sweeps as recomputable (only the cached journal is discarded), but the inconsistency with the project-delete confirm pattern is a minor foot-gun.

findings.title: Alignment sub-tab can render blank when a run yields zero records
findings.evidence: CompareView only mounts AlignmentView when alignmentRecords.length > 0 (CompareView.tsx:259); the 'Ready to align' empty state also requires alignmentRecords.length === 0 (line 233). After an alignment that returns zero records, jobStatus is no longer 'idle', so neither branch matches and the Alignment panel area shows nothing under the header.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit 'Alignment ran but found no aligned passages' state for the alignment sub-view when a completed run produced zero records, so the outcome is legible rather than an empty panel.
